The Little Movement is the canonical works-table record for PKD's short-story collection corpus item. The record links the archive's preserved manifestation of the work to the broader corpus and gives researchers a single place to follow its bibliographic and interpretive context.

The preserved archive item here is The Little Movement (Unknown).

The source record itself summarizes the work as follows: A 9-page scanned PDF of 'The Little Movement,' a short story by Philip K. Dick. No OCR text layer is present. 'The Little Movement' is a known Dick short story from his early career, published in Fantasy and Science Fiction magazine in November 1952.

The story is one of Dick's earliest published science fiction stories, written during the explosive burst of productivity that launched his professional career. At 9 scanned pages, this document preserves the story in its original published format. 'The Little Movement' demonstrates the themes of animation, autonomy, and the blurring of boundaries between the living and the mechanical that would become hallmarks of Dick's mature fiction.

The entry is most useful when tracing publication context, later commentary, or relationships to other works.
